title: Malachi
summary: Malachi is a biblical book focused on covenant faithfulness, temple worship, priestly rebuke, and coming judgment.
historical_context: Malachi confronts post-exilic covenant apathy and looks toward the Lord's coming day.
ancient_near_east_context: Malachi belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Malachi should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Malachi as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Minor Prophets, book 12 of 12, Malachi contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting covenant faithfulness, temple worship, priestly rebuke, and coming judgment to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Malachi as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Malachi uses prophecy within Minor Prophets, book 12 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Malachi helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars recognize collection and editorial shaping
date_ranges: 8th-5th centuries BCE, depending on the prophet
Final forms often reflect later collection and editing
original_audience: Israel and Judah under covenant accountability before and after exile
historical_setting: Assyrian, Babylonian, and post-exilic settings across the prophetic corpus
canonical_role: Malachi anchors covenant faithfulness, temple worship, priestly rebuke, and coming judgment within Minor Prophets, book 12 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How to read prophetic poetry, irony, and symbolic action
